license.changes: Mapped geometry and annotations converted to umbra scene coordinates; other same-recording LiDAR sweeps registered into measured triangles. Scoring sweep excluded; holes retained. No endorsement implied.

limitations: One frame; no independent reference. Mapped ground is publisher terrain inside mapped drivable areas, not observed road.
The crossing is the mapped near edge on the current vehicle centre line; its error is the map-to-paint offset (crossingError), which never moves it.
A point labeled mapped, not observed has no camera-visible LiDAR return agreeing with the map within 0.5 m (for example in the LiDAR shadow).
A hidden point lies behind an annotated object in the image: the pixel shows that object, not the ground.
Annotated objects other than the current vehicle are from the LiDAR sweep about 40 ms before the image; the current stationary vehicle is the average of all its annotations in the log.
The person position and height are declared defaults, not detections.

Each object is evaluated at the exact floating projection of its mapped point (pixelUV); the integer pixel only anchors display and small edits. pixelOffsetFromMappedM is internal consistency, not accuracy.

The along-ray uncertainty uses a fixed height band fitted on development scenes (8c52d911/2658849 app scene (grounded-v3.4, placement protocol v3.4)); this scene's LiDAR ground returns only test it (heldOutResiduals); it describes the mapped-ground height error along the pixel ray, not the crossing position or a physical accuracy bound.
Placements more than 30 m from the camera (horizontal) are refused.

The mapped-edge crossing model applies only when both crossing edges are ahead of the camera, the near edge is within 45 degrees of perpendicular to the lane, and the centre line meets the mapped near edge segment ahead of the camera; otherwise the crossing, and the vehicle, person and curb anchored on it, stay Unknown with the named refusal.
Geometric visibility only, never Clear; not a safety, recognition or compliance judgment.
